mechaber/1:main: Laws of Purim meal. Containing 4 paragraphs One who does the Purim meal at night does not fulfill his obligation. {Rama: It is a mitzvah to have many feasts during Purim (Tur), but one fulfills his obligation with only one feast (Mordechai} {Rama: Nevertheless, one should be happy and add more during his meal even at night (Teshuvat Mahariv}.}
mechaber/2:main: One is obligated to be intoxicated on Purim to the point where he does not know [the difference] between "accursed is Haman" and "blessed is Mordechai". {Rama: Some say it is not necessary to become drunk so much, but rather to drink more than he is used to (Kol Bo), and to fall asleep, and while he sleeps he does not know [the difference] between "accursed is Haman" and "blessed is Mordechai" (Maharil). [There is no difference on Purim] between one who has more and one who has less, as long as his heart is directed to heaven. One should not fast on Purim, except for a fast for a [bad] dream, and see earlier Siman 568 and Siman 570. There are those who have the custom to dress in Shabbat/Yom Tov clothes on Purim, and that is correct (Maharil). We have the custom to make the Purim meal after the afternoon prayer, and pray the evening prayer at night. We pray the afternoon prayer while most of the day remains, and most of the meal needs to be during the day (Minhagim). And it should not be like those who have the custom to start close to evening, and most of the meal happens during the night of the 15th. When Purim falls out on Friday, they should have the meal in the morning because of honor for the Shabbat (Minhagim). And one who wants to [have his meal] every [Purim] in the morning is allowed to (T"H). Some say that there is [significance] to eating seeds on Purim as a remembrance for the seeds that Daniel and his friends ate in Babylonia (Kol Bo). It is good to delve a bit in Torah before one begins the meal, and a support for that is (Esther 8:16) "The Jews had light and happiness...", which we learn out "radiance" - that's Torah (Mahariv). One is obligated to drink a little and be a little happy on two days, the 14th and the 15th (Minhagim}, and so is the custom. And some say that if one causes damage to his fellow through his happiness on Purim, he is exempt from restitution (Terumat HaDeshen, Part I 110}. And see Terumat HaDeshen Laws of Damages.}
mechaber/3:main: One says "Al hanisim" in the Grace After Meals during the blessing of the land ["Nodeh"]. And if one started his meal during the day, and extended it into the night, he [still] says "al hanisim", for we follow the [status of] the beginning of the meal. And some say one should not say it. (And we have the custom like the first opinion).
mechaber/4:main: One must send to his fellow two portions of meat, or foodstuffs, as it says (Esther 9:19) "And send portions, man to his fellow." Two portions to one man [is the obligation]. And anyone who send more to his fellows is praiseworthy. If he has none, he can trade with his fellow, this one sending to that one his meal, and this one sending to that one his meal, so that they can fulfill "And send portions, man to his fellow." {Rama: And some send the portions during the day and not at night (from the Rosh, first chapter of [Bavli] Megilla}. And if one sends portions to his fellow, but he doesn't want to accept them, or he forgives him [his obligation], he fulfills [his obligation nonetheless]. And a woman is obligated in [sending] portions to the destitute and sending portions [to one's fellows] like a man is. A woman sends to a woman, a man to a man. But not the other way, so that a man does not come to send it to a widow, and it will come to a possibility of kiddushin [having been enacted]. But portions to the destitute one should not worry [about this possibility].}

turei-zahav/2:א: (א) A person must become intoxicated etc. Many wish to answer and explain what the intent is here and it was not settled; in my humble opinion to explain thus: a person must give praise to the Blessed One for double good He did for us — first punishment He brought on Haman, and had Mordechai not been blessed but saved with all Israel we would have been satisfied; rather He blessed Mordechai with very great honor and extra good — therefore he said one must become intoxicated until he does not know our superiority of cursed is Haman which is his humiliation to blessed is Mordechai which is our second superiority; the intent from saying until he does not know implies before his intoxication he knew and gave thanks for this — they intended he should not cease giving thanks for this in joy until he comes to not distinguishing anymore, and then he is exempt from this in my humble opinion.
turei-zahav/2:ב: (ב) And some say he need not become drunk etc. The statement of Rava in gemara until he does not know etc. is rejected by this statement, since in gemara he brings on this Rabbah who slaughtered R' Zeira — we learn from gemara conclusion one should not do so much; Beit Yosef in name of Ran in name of R' Efraim.

turei-zahav/4:ב: (ב) Exchange with his friend. In gemara they say Abbaye bar Avin and R' Chanina bar Avin exchange their meals reciprocally; Ran explained neither was able to send and leave for himself, therefore each sends his meal to the other to eat Purim meal and fulfill mishloach manot; this way is written here; Rashi explained they exchange meals — this one eats with that one on Purim this year and second year his friend feasts with him; Beit Yosef challenged Rashi's explanation: if so they did not fulfill mishloach manot ish lere'ehu; you could say they sent portions ish lere'ehu — what does it teach? End of his words; in my humble opinion for Rashi it was a novelty they said explicitly this one will eat with this one and then reverse, and one could say it was like a loan and there is no manot here since gift specifically — it teaches nevertheless they fulfilled, meaning this year this one fulfilled by inviting his friend and his friend sent to another person, and second year the reverse; but one must be exact: why did Rashi not explain truly all on one year and both fulfilled? Perhaps one could say then it was truly complete loan since all see immediately he receives payment and there was condition between them — not so if in two years it would not appear like payment this year and not that; example for this we find (Yoreh Deah) siman 170 s.k. 2 in Hagahah: one should not say to his friend come eat with me what you fed me, for it is like paying his debt and appears as if he loaned him, and concern he will feed him more and there is interest; but permitted to say come eat with me and I will eat with you another time, and permitted to eat with him even a greater meal — end. Behold at second eating it is forbidden to mention it is payment — so too here then it was loan in my correct opinion.
